Opposite Party/s  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Priyesh Kumar Jaiswal  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Humayou Ahmad Khan  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR SINHA  ORAL ORDER 2 19-10-2023 1.
Heard learned Counsel for the petitioners and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. This application, for grant of anticipatory bail, arises out of Ahiyapur Police Station Case No. 288 of 2023, disclosing offences under Sections 406, 420, 323, 504, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 138 of the N.I. Act.

3. As per the First Information Report, the petitioner gave seven cheques, totaling Rs. 25 lacs, to the informant as a consideration amount for purchase of the piece of land situated in Khesra No. 3252 having an area of 3.75 decimals and 5 decimals.
But upon presentation of the cheque for encashment, all the cheques were dishonored due to insufficient fund.

Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.63787 of 2023(2) dt.19-10-2023 4.
Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have falsely been implicated in the present case with oblique motive.

Learned counsel next submits that Section 138 of the N.I. Act is not made out in view of the fact that for bouncing of the cheque, no complaint adhering to the timeline, as prescribed in the Act, has been lodged by the informant, rather, the informant has Kanchan Kumari vs The State Of Bihar on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112197743/
1 lodged the First Information Report.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submits that there was an agreement for sale between the petitioners and the informant under which the petitioners were required to pay a sum of Rs. 43 lacs and odd amount which has already been paid by the petitioners.
The same would be evident from Annexure-3 series which are the bank transactions receipt of transferring the consideration amount by the petitioners in favour of the informant.
The money receipt, duly executed by the informant, is part of Annexure-3 Series at Page 27 of this application.

5. Having regard to the submissions made on behalf of the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the present FIR has been lodged arising out of land transactions between the parties and petitioners claim to have paid all the consideration amount in favour of the informant, I am inclined to grant the petitioner privilege of anticipatory bail.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.63787 of 2023(2) dt.19-10-2023 6.

7. Let the petitioner, Kanchan Kumari, Dipak Kumar @ Deepak Kumar, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the Court below within four weeks, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Muzaffarpur, in connection with Ahiyapur Police Station Case No. 288 of 2023, subject to the condition laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
(Anil Kumar Sinha, J) HarshPandey/-
